The [United States of America](/wiki/United_States "United States") has sent [athletes](/wiki/Athlete "Athlete") to every celebration of the modern [Olympic Games](/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") with the exception of the [1980 Summer Olympics](/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics"), during which it led a [boycott](/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1980 Summer Olympics boycott") in protest of the [Soviet Union's invasion of Afghanistan](/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War "Soviet–Afghan War"). The [United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee](/wiki/United_States_Olympic_%26_Paralympic_Committee "United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee") (USOPC) is the [National Olympic Committee](/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") for the United States.

The United States have been the host nation for the modern Olympics on eight occasions. The [2028 Summer Olympics](/wiki/2028_Summer_Olympics "2028 Summer Olympics") will be held in [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), upping the tally to nine.

American athletes have won a total of 2,765 medals (1,105 of them gold) at the [Summer Olympic Games](/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games"), and another 363 (126 of them gold) at the [Winter Olympic Games](/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"), making the United States the most prolific medal-winning nation in the history of the Olympics. The U.S. has placed first in the Summer Olympic medal table [19 times out of 30 Summer Olympics](/wiki/List_of_Olympic_teams_by_medals_won#List_by_team "List of Olympic teams by medals won") and 29 appearances (having boycotted in 1980), but has had less success in the Winter Olympics, placing first [once in 24 participations](/wiki/List_of_Olympic_teams_by_medals_won#List_by_team_2 "List of Olympic teams by medals won").[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]

Along with the Orinoco, the Amazon is one of the main habitats of the *[boto](/wiki/Boto "Boto")*, also known as the [Amazon river dolphin](/wiki/Amazon_river_dolphin "Amazon river dolphin") (*Inia geoffrensis*). It is the largest species of [river dolphin](/wiki/River_dolphin "River dolphin"), and it can grow to lengths of up to 2.6 m (8.5 ft). The colour of its skin changes with age; young animals are gray, but become pink and then white as they mature. The dolphins use [echolocation](/wiki/Animal_echolocation "Animal echolocation") to navigate and hunt in the river's tricky depths.[[94]](#cite_note-98) The *boto* is the subject of a legend in Brazil about a [dolphin](/wiki/Dolphin "Dolphin") that turns into a man and seduces maidens by the riverside.[[95]](#cite_note-99)

The [tucuxi](/wiki/Tucuxi "Tucuxi") (*Sotalia fluviatilis*), also a dolphin species, is found both in the rivers of the Amazon basin and in the coastal waters of South America. The [Amazonian manatee](/wiki/Amazonian_manatee "Amazonian manatee") (*Trichechus inunguis*), also known as "seacow", is found in the northern Amazon River basin and its tributaries. It is a mammal and a herbivore. Its population is limited to freshwater habitats, and, unlike other manatees, it does not venture into saltwater. *Star Wars: The Force Awakens* grossed $936.7 million in the United States and Canada and $1.132 billion in other countries for a worldwide total of $2.07 billion,[[3]](#cite_note-BOM-3) making it the [highest-grossing film of 2015](/wiki/2015_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2015 in film")[[293]](#cite_note-Top2015Films-297) and the [third highest-grossing film of all time](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films "List of highest-grossing films").[[294]](#cite_note-298) [Box Office Mojo](/wiki/Box_Office_Mojo "Box Office Mojo") estimates that the film sold close to 110 million tickets in the United States and Canada.[[295]](#cite_note-299) *The Force Awakens* earned 8.6% of the total 2015 releases in the United States and Canada, second only to the 8.8% of the box office earned by *[Titanic](/wiki/Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* in 1997.[[296]](#cite_note-300) It was the 24th film in cinematic history to gross $1 billion worldwide, standing as the [fastest film](/wiki/List_of_fastest-grossing_films "List of fastest-grossing films") to surpass the mark at the time, doing so in 12 days.[[297]](#cite_note-fastest-to-1b-301) It was also the third film in history to surpass $2 billion worldwide, doing so on its 53rd day of release.[[298]](#cite_note-302) *Deadline Hollywood* calculated the film's net profit as $780.1 million, accounting for production budgets,[[e]](#cite_note-303) marketing, talent participations, and other costs; box office grosses and home media revenues placed it first on their list of 2015's "Most Valuable Blockbusters".[[173]](#cite_note-DeadlineProfitAnalysisFinal-177)
